questions.q: In 'The Man and the Lion', what did the statue in the clearing show?
choices: Heracles tearing the jaws of a Lion
A Lion chasing a frightened Man
A Lion and a Man as good friends
A King sitting high on a golden throne
questions.evidence: Heracles in the act of tearing the jaws of the Nemean Lion

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Man and the Lion'?
choices: It depends on who tells the story
Men are much stronger than lions
Never travel through the forest
Statues always tell the truth
questions.evidence: It all depends on the point of view, and who tells the story.

questions.q: In 'The Ass and the Lap Dog', why did the Ass go into the house and act like the Dog?
choices: He was jealous and wanted the Master's favor
He was hungry and wanted the Master's dinner
He was scared of the dark stable at night
The servants had told him to come inside
questions.evidence: the jealous Ass got it into his silly head

questions.q: In 'The Ass and the Lap Dog', what happened after the Ass put his feet on the Master's knees?
choices: The chair tipped over and they fell into broken dishes
The Master laughed and patted him kindly on his gray head
The Lap Dog barked and chased him out of the house
The Master gave him a sweet treat from the table
questions.evidence: Ass and man rolled over together in the pile of broken dishes

questions.q: What is one lesson of 'The Ass and the Lap Dog'?
choices: Do not try to win favor by acting against your nature
Dogs will always make better pets than donkeys do
Always stay in your stable and never visit the house
Masters love clumsy animals the most of all their pets
questions.evidence: Do not try to gain favor by acting in a way that is contrary to your own nature and character.

questions.q: In 'The Milkmaid and Her Pail', what did the Milkmaid plan to buy with the money from her butter?
choices: Eggs for hatching
A pretty new dress
A young brown cow
A new milk pail
questions.evidence: I will buy a lot of eggs for hatching

questions.q: In 'The Milkmaid and Her Pail', why did the milk spill?
choices: She tossed her head and the pail fell
She tripped on a rock in the road
A cow bumped into her on the path
The old pail had a hole in the bottom
questions.evidence: she tossed her head scornfully, and down fell the pail of milk

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Milkmaid and Her Pail'?
choices: Do not count your chickens before they are hatched
Always carry your milk pail in your hands, not on your head
Butter will always sell well at the market in town
Wear your new dress to the fair to catch everyone's eye
questions.evidence: Do not count your chickens before they are hatched.

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the Shepherd' at the end of this chapter, what bothered the Wolf?
choices: People chased him for eating a lamb but ate one themselves
The Shepherd did not invite him in to share the dinner
The lamb the family was eating had been burned black
The family in the hut was much too loud for him to sleep
questions.evidence: had they caught me at just the very thing they are doing
